'''Anthony Fieldings''' (born July 9, 1971) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Buffalo Bills]] and [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He also was a member of the [[Rhein Fire (NFL Europe)|Rhein Fire]] in the [[NFL Europe|World League of American Football]] (WLAF). He played [[college football]] for the [[Morningside Mustangs football|Morningside Mustangs]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FielAn20.htm |title=Anthony Fieldings NFL Football Statistics |publisher=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |accessdate=June 10, 2012}}</ref>

==Early life==
Fieldings attended [[Eustis High School]]. He accepted a football scholarship from [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[Morningside University|Morningside College]]. As a junior in 1991, he was a starter at [[inside linebacker]] and set a school single-season record with 151 tackles.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/223249784/ | title=NCC | access-date=August 29, 2021}}</ref> He also set a school single-game record with 24 tackles against the [[University of South Dakota]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/337304837/ | title=Sports | access-date=August 29, 2021}}</ref> He left as the school's all-time leader in career tackles.

==Professional career==
Fieldings was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Buffalo Bills]] after the [[1993 NFL draft]] on May 7.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/05/08/sports/transactions-349993.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=8 May 1993 | access-date=August 29, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on August 24.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/08/25/sports/transactions-872293.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=25 August 1993 | access-date=August 29, 2021}}</ref> On December 30, 1993, he was re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/12/31/sports/transactions-181193.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=31 December 1993 | access-date=August 29, 2021}}</ref> He was released on August 22, 1994.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/08/23/sports/transactions-037664.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=23 August 1994 | access-date=August 29, 2021}}</ref>

On July 31, 1995, he signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He was a reserve player, registering one defensive tackle and 5 [[special teams]] tackles. He appeared in 4 games and was released on October 4. The team would go on to win [[Super Bowl XXX]].

In 1998, he was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]]. He was released on June 9.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/273491629/ | title=Transactions | access-date=August 29, 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2016, he was a part of a group of former players that filed a [[civil suit]] against the [[NFL]], requesting it to recognize brain injury disease for workers' compensation.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/fl-nfl-workers-comp-20161121-story.html | title=Former NFL players file civil suit asking NFL to recognize brain injury disease for workers' comp | access-date=August 29, 2021 | archive-date=October 5, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005033238/https://www.baltimoresun.com/fl-nfl-workers-comp-20161121-story.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Anthony Harris''' (born October 9, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia Cavaliers]], and was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2015. He played his first six seasons with Minnesota, and was the NFL [[interception]]s co-leader in 2019.

==Early life==
Harris attended [[Lloyd C. Bird High School]] in [[Chesterfield, Virginia]], where he played [[quarterback]], [[wide receiver]] and [[defensive back]] (two-time All-state and All-region selection). As a junior, he allowed only one completion and notched eight [[interceptions]] on defense, while also throwing for over 1,000 yards and [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushing]] for 800 more yards from the quarterback spot on offense. In 2010, he was selected to the first-team All-Group AAA football team by the [[Associated Press]] (AP) and was named to the All-Dominion District first-team as a utility player and earned All-district second-team accolades at both quarterback and defensive back. Harris was also a starter on the Skyhawk [[high school basketball|basketball]] team as well.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/anthony_harris_799742.html |title=Anthony Harris Bio - VirginiaSports.com - University of Virginia Official Athletics Website - UVA Cavaliers Football |access-date=December 17, 2013 |archive-date=January 10, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180110034550/http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/anthony_harris_799742.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Regarded as a three-star prospect according to both [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]], Harris was ranked as the No. 34 athlete in the nation and No. 13 recruit in the state of [[Virginia]] by Rivals. He was ranked as the No. 68 [[wide receiver]] in the country by Scout. He also received a scouts grade of 72 from [[ESPN.com]] and was ranked the No. 201 athlete in nation. Harris committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Virginia]] on June 2, 2010, after being recruited by then head coach [[Jim Reid (American football)|Jim Reid]]. He chose the Cavaliers over scholarship offers from [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland]], [[Richmond Spiders football|Richmond]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia]], among others.

==College career==
Harris attended the [[University of Virginia]], where he played for the [[Virginia Cavaliers football]] team from 2011 to 2014. He started 35 of the 49 games he played at Virginia. Harris ended his collegiate career with 289 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] (145 solo and 6 for loss), 11 [[interception]]s, 2 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], 2 forced [[fumble]]s and 19 [[passes defensed]]. His 11 interceptions tied him for No. 10 all-time in program history.

In his first season in 2011, Harris was one of 12 [[true freshmen]] to appear in games for the Cavaliers, playing in all 13 of Virginia's games. He appeared mostly on [[special teams]] and finished the season with 14 total tackles including a season-high three stops at [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]].

As a sophomore in 2012, Harris helped anchor the nation's youngest starting secondary, which featured 4 sophomores and 1 freshman. Harris recorded 87 total tackles (48 solo and 0.5 for loss), a forced fumble, an interception and was credited with 3 passes defensed. He was one of 11 Cavaliers to start all 12 games. He made his first career interception at [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State]] and returned it for 37 yards. He registered four games with double-digit tackles, with 11 against [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]], 12 against [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech]], 10 at [[Duke Blue Devils football|Duke]] and had a career-high 14 tackles against [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]]. Against Louisiana Tech, he helped hold one of the nation's most prolific offenses to its lowest output of total yards (385 yards) on the season and only game the Bulldogs were held under 400 yards.

As a junior in 2013, Harris started 11 games for the Cavaliers, earned first-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) honors and was an [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' after leading the nation in interceptions with eight, the most by a Cavalier since [[Ronde Barber]] led the ACC with eight in 1994.<ref>[http://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-football-notes-harris-on-acc-coaches-first-team/article_d7b89dd8-62b1-11e3-8d2e-0019bb30f31a.html Virginia football notes: Harris on ACC coaches' first team]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131219021004/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-football/news/20131217/college-football-all-america-team/?eref=sihp Jameis Winston, Aaron Donald lead SI.com's 2013 All-America Team]</ref> Harris finished the season with 80 total tackles (42 solo and 3.5 for loss), one sack, a forced fumble, six passes defensed and eight interceptions, which placed Harris No. 2 all-time at Virginia for interceptions in a season, tied with Ronde Barber and Kevin Cook. He also blocked a key punt in the second half of Virginia's victory against [[BYU Cougars football|BYU]] and was named the Walter Camp National Defensive Player of the Week for his efforts against the Cougars.

In his final season at Virginia in 2014, Harris was named 3rd-Team All-ACC. Harris notched a career-high 108 tackles (No. 5 in the ACC and No. 31 in the nation) along with two interceptions, a sack and ten passes defensed. He had eight tackles, broke up one pass and returned one interception for seven yards in Virginia's win against No. 21 [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville]] to earn the first of his two ACC Defensive Back of the Week honors, with the second one coming in a win over [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]] in which he recorded 10 tackles and broke up three passes. He had 13 tackles against [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pitt]], including one sack for a loss of 11 yards. He ended the year with seven tackles in the season finale at [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]].

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On December 1, 2014, it was announced that Harris had accepted his invitation to play in the [[2015 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2014 |title=Third group of players pushes roster to 63 |url=https://www.seniorbowl.com/news-highlights-detail.php?news=249 |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=seniorbowl.com}}</ref> Unfortunately, he was unable to participate after discovering he had sustained a torn [[Glenoid labrum|labrum]] during his senior season that would require surgery. Harris attended the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]], but was limited to the [[40-yard dash]] due to his injury. He had private visits with representatives from the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[New York Giants]], and [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dave Birkett |date=April 21, 2015 |title=Lions host Virginia safety on draft visit |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2015/04/21/anthony-harris-virginia/26105037/ |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=freep.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Carl Knowles |date=April 23, 2014 |title=Anthony Harris, A safety on the mend |url=http://vikingsterritory.com/2015/nfl-draft-2015/anthony-harris-a-safety-on-the-mend |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=vikingsterritory.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2015 |title=Virginia safety Anthony Harris has pre-draft visit with Giants, per source |url=https://www.nj.com/articles/15761402/virginia_safety_anthony_harris_has_pre-draft_visit.amp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215054544/https://www.nj.com/articles/15761402/virginia_safety_anthony_harris_has_pre-draft_visit.amp |archive-date=December 15, 2017 |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=nj.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Harris received a wide range of varying draft projections due to his shoulder injury. He was projected by [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts to possibly go as early as the second round or as late as the seventh. The majority of draft experts and scouts projected him to be a third or fourth round pick. He was ranked the fourth best [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] prospect by NFL analyst [[Charles Davis (defensive back)|Charles Davis]], the fifth best safety by NFL analyst [[Bucky Brooks]], and was ranked the ninth best free safety in the draft by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Harris, DS #9 FS, Virginia |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=119960&draftyear=2015&genpos=fs |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Charles Davis |date=April 7, 2015 |title=2015 NFL Draft prospect rankings by position |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/2015-nfl-draft-prospect-rankings-by-position-0ap3000000483055 |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bucky Brooks |date=February 25, 2015 |title=Brooks: Top five 2015 NFL Draft prospects by position |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/brooks-top-five-2015-nfl-draft-prospects-by-position-0ap3000000473871 |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
====2015 season====
On May 2, 2015, the [[Minnesota Vikings]] signed Harris as an [[undrafted free agent]] after he was not one of the 15 safeties selected during the [[2015 NFL draft]]. The Vikings signed him to a three-year, $1.58 million [[contract]] that includes a $10,000 [[signing bonus]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Anthony Harris contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/anthony-harris-17018/ |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> Harris going undrafted surprised many scouts and analysts, due to the 2015 NFL draft being very thin at the safety position with only four true safeties being selected in the first two rounds. His fall in the draft was attributed to his shoulder injury and many reporting his recovery process could possibly extend into the beginning of the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why Undrafted?: Anthony Harris |url=http://walterfootball.com/wu2015aharris.php |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=WalterFootball.com}}</ref> ESPN analyst [[Todd McShay]] listed Harris as the top undrafted free agent after the draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chris Burke |date=May 5, 2015 |title=The next Wes Welker: Finney, Harris among top undrafted free agents |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2015/05/06/undrafted-free-agents-bj-finney-anthony-harris |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=si.com}}</ref>

Throughout his first [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Harris competed against [[Andrew Sendejo]], [[Antone Exum]], and [[Robert Blanton]] for the starting strong safety position. On September 5, 2015, he was waived by the Minnesota Vikings, but was re-signed to the [[practice squad]] the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Isaac Schweer |date=September 6, 2015 |title=Vikings Re-Sign 9 to Practice Squad |url=http://wjon.com/vikings-re-sign-9-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=wjon.com}}</ref>

On December 8, 2015, Harris was promoted to the active roster after spending the first 12 games on the practice squad. He was named the starting free safety, alongside cornerback [[Terrence Newman]], after multiple injuries to safeties [[Harrison Smith]], Sendejo, and Exum. On December 10, 2015, Harris made his first career start and professional regular season debut during a 23–20 loss to the [[Arizona Cardinals]] and led the team with eight combined tackles while also deflecting a deep pass attempt by [[Carson Palmer]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eric Oslund |date=December 13, 2015 |title=Harris shows promise at safety for Minnesota |url=https://scout.com/nfl/vikings/Article/Anthony-Harris-shows-promise-at-safety-for-Minnesota-Vikings-75024751 |access-date=December 14, 2017 |website=scout.com}}</ref> The following game, he made his second consecutive start and collected five combined tackles and defended a pass in a 38–17 victory over the [[Chicago Bears]]. He finished his rookie season with 15 combined tackles (12 solo) and two pass deflections in four games and two starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Harris |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyharris/2553655/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

The Vikings completed the 2015 season with an 11–5 record and finished atop the [[NFC North]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Minnesota Vikings Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/min/2015.htm |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On January 10, 2016, Harris appeared in his first career playoff game as the Vikings lost 10–9 to the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the [[National Football Conference|NFC]] Wild Card Round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Seattle Seahawks at Minnesota Vikings - January 10th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601100min.htm |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2016 season====
Harris entered training camp competing for a job as the backup safety against [[Michael Griffin (American football)|Michael Griffin]], Exum, and [[Jayron Kearse]]. Head coach [[Mike Zimmer]] named Harris the backup free safety to Smith to begin the 2016 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Minnesota Vikings depth chart: 10/01/2016 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/188/MIN |access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref>

On December 11, 2016, Harris started at free safety in place of an injured Smith who suffered a severe high ankle sprain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=December 7, 2016 |title=Report: Harrison Smith could miss rest of regular season |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/report-harrison-smith-ankle-possibly-out-for-season-0ap3000000752938 |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He recorded seven solo tackles in a 25–16 victory at the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. The next week, Harris collected a career-high 15 combined tackles and defended a pass as the Vikings were routed 34–6 by the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. On January 1, 2017, he started at strong safety in place of Sendejo who injured his knee during practice. Harris went on to make eight combined tackles in a 38–10 victory over the Bears.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tasman |first=Kyle |date=December 31, 2016 |title=Andrew Sendejo placed on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.247sports.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/Bolt/Andrew-Sendejo-injury-Minnesota-Vikings--50159620/Amp |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=247sports.com}}{{dead link|date=January 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He finished the season with 30 combined tackles (11 solo) and a pass deflection and played in 16 games with three starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Harris (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyharris/2553655/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2017 season====
Harris began the 2017 regular season as the backup free safety to Smith. On October 15, 2017, against the [[Green Bay Packers]], he started at strong safety after Sendejo was sidelined with a [[groin]] injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yotter |first=Tim |date=October 23, 2017 |title=Sendejo inactive, Packers missing starters |url=https://www.scout.com/nfl/vikings/Article/Andrew-Sendejo-inactive-for-Minnesota-Vikings-Green-Bay-Packers-missing-starters-108971555/Amp |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=scout.com}}</ref> He recorded two solo tackles in a 23–10 victory for Minnesota. Due to Sendejo being suspended for a Week 8 matchup against the [[Cleveland Browns]] in London, Harris got the start again and recovered a fumble by running back [[Isaiah Crowell]] in the third quarter. During a Week 11 matchup against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Harris recorded a season-high seven combined tackles after starting at strong safety with Sendejo inactive due to a groin and hamstring injury. Harris also deflected a pass, as the Vikings defeated the Rams 24–7.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yotter |first=Tim |date=November 23, 2017 |title=Sendejo returns for Vikings, Lions make Ansah active |url=https://www.scout.com/nfl/vikings/Article/Andrew-Sendejo-returns-for-Minnesota-Vikings-Detroit-Lions-make-Ziggy-Ansah-active-110939291/Amp |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=scout.com}}</ref>

====2018 season====
On March 8, 2018, Harris re-signed with the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=March 8, 2018 |title=Vikings will hold onto Anthony Harris |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/08/vikings-will-hold-onto-anthony-harris/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref> In Week 6 against the Cardinals, Harris recorded his first career interception off quarterback [[Josh Rosen]] in the 27–17 win. In Week 11 against the Bears, Harris intercepted [[Mitchell Trubisky]] twice in a 25–20 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 19, 2018 |title=In loss to Bears, Anthony Harris makes his case at safety |url=https://www.skornorth.com/vikings-2/2018/11/loss-bears-anthony-harris-makes-case-safety/ |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=SKOR North |language=en-US}}</ref>

====2019 season====
On March 11, 2019, the Vikings placed a second-round restricted free agent tender on Harris.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 11, 2019 |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-announce-roster-moves-031119 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> Following the release of Sendejo, Harris was named a starting safety alongside Smith.

In Week 1 against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], Harris intercepted [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] twice and recovered a fumble as the Vikings won 28–12.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2019 |title=Vikings trample Falcons 28-12 behind fierce defense, Cook |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127961 |access-date=September 8, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> For his Week 1 effort, Harris was awarded NFC Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2019 |title=Lamar Jackson, Dak Prescott among Players of the Week |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001053523/article/lamar-jackson-dak-prescott-among-players-of-the-week |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190914133822/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001053523/article/lamar-jackson-dak-prescott-among-players-of-the-week |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 14, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>
In Week 8 against the [[Washington Redskins]], Harris recorded his third interception of the season off [[Dwayne Haskins]] in the 19–9 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2019 |title=Cook, Vikings wear down Redskins 19-9 for 4th straight win |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127905 |access-date=October 24, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> On December 2, 2019, against the Seahawks, Harris intercepted [[Russell Wilson]] and returned it 20 yards for his first career [[touchdown]] in the 37–30 loss. Harris would record two more interceptions throughout the season, which came off [[Philip Rivers]] in a 39–10 win over the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], and [[Aaron Rodgers]] in a 23–10 loss to the Packers. With six interceptions, Harris was tied for the NFL's most alongside New England's [[Stephon Gilmore]] and Buffalo's [[Tre'Davious White]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.twincities.com/2019/12/31/for-first-time-in-16-years-the-vikings-have-an-nfl-interception-leader-with-anthony-harris/|title=For first time in 16 years, Vikings have an NFL interception leader: Anthony Harris|date=December 31, 2019}}</ref>

[[File:Anthony Harris (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Harris with the Eagles in 2021]]

In the NFC Wild Card game against the [[New Orleans Saints]], Harris intercepted a pass thrown by [[Drew Brees]] and returned it for 30 yards during the 26–20 overtime win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2020 |title=Cook, Vikings upend Saints 26-20 in OT in NFC playoffs |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131038 |access-date=January 5, 2020 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2020 season====
On March 16, 2020, the Vikings placed the franchise tag on Harris.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook, Nick |date=March 16, 2020 |title=Vikings use franchise tag to keep Anthony Harris |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/vikings-use-franchise-tag-to-keep-anthony-harris-0ap3000001106387 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He signed his franchise tender on May 18, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith, Eric |date=May 18, 2020 |title=Anthony Harris Signs Franchise Tender Offer |work=Vikings.com |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/anthony-harris-signs-franchise-tender-offer |access-date=May 26, 2020}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles (first stint)===
Harris signed a one-year $5 million contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on March 20, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31096087/ex-vikings-safety-anthony-harris-agrees-1-year-5-million-deal-eagles|title=Ex-Vikings S Harris headed to Eagles, agent says |date=March 19, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson, Chris |date=March 20, 2021 |title=Eagles add S Anthony Harris, the right 'fit' on defense |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-add-anthony-harris |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> In week 6, he caught his first and only interception of the season off a pass from Tom Brady during the 22–28 loss to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web| title= Anthony Harris Game Logs | website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HarrAn01/gamelog/}}</ref>

J. Gardner-Johnson]], and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles announce initial 53-man roster|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-202|author=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=August 30, 2022}}{{Dead link|date=September 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles sign 15 players to the practice squad|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-15-players-to-the-practice-squad|author=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=August 31, 2022}}</ref> On September 5, the Eagles and Harris mutually agreed to terminate his practice squad contract to maximize Harris' flexibility to join other teams' active rosters.<ref name="l077">{{cite web | last=Erby | first=Glenn | title=Eagles and Anthony Harris agree to part way | website=Eagles Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2022-09-05 | url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/eagles/2022/09/05/philadelphia-eagles-terminate-anthony-harris-practice-squad-contract-nfl-free-agency/80558831007/ | access-date=2025-03-09}}</ref>

'''Anthony Hitchens''' (born June 10, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]] and was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fourth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Hitchens was raised by his mother, Norma Hitchens, in [[Lorain, Ohio]], where he attended [[Clearview High School (Lorain, Ohio)|Clearview High School]]. He has six siblings and does not have a relationship with his father who was in and out of prison. At the age of 12, Hitchens asked his mother if he could move in with his best friend, Zach Anderson, and his family in [[Sheffield Township, Lorain County, Ohio|Sheffield Township]]. His mother gave him her permission and he immediately moved into Brad and Amy Anderson's home. Brad attended high school with Norma and Amy worked at a nonprofit organization in the community with her. Anthony played [[American football|football]] with their oldest son Zach and would stay overnight and always eat dinner with them. Amy Anderson said there was no discussion about letting him move in because they both cared for him. With two sons of their own and another friend, James Washington, living there, the Andersons added an additional room so the boys would no longer have to share one room among the four of them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=David Moore |title=How Anthony Hitchens' decision at age 12 eventually made him Dallas Cowboy |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboys/2014/05/17/how-one-player-s-decision-at-age-12-eventually-made-him-a-dallas-cowboy |access-date=December 9, 2017 |website=sportsday.Dallasnews.com}}</ref>

In high school, Hitchens was a three-sport athlete, playing football, [[basketball]], and [[Track and field|track]]. On the football field he was also known for being an explosive [[running back]]. He is the school's all-time [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushing]] leader with 3,864 yards, and the single game leader with 354 yards.

Hitchens was labeled a two-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]''.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/iowa/football/recruiting/player-Anthony-Hitchens-99558 Anthony Hitchens – Yahoo Sports]</ref> He had offers from the [[University of Kansas]], [[Indiana University]], [[University of Akron]], and [[Eastern Michigan]], before deciding to continue his career at the [[University of Iowa]].

==College career==
At Iowa, Hitchens was a four-year [[letter winner]]. In his first two years, he stayed mainly on [[special teams]], before starting at [[linebacker]] as a junior and senior. In his career at Iowa he racked up 270 total [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], including 124 as a junior which led the [[Big Ten Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Hitchens College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-hitchens-1.html |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Hitchens was one of 35 linebackers to perform at the [[NFL Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana|Indianapolis]]. Although he performed all of the combine drills, his day was considered mediocre. He tied for 12th among his position group in the [[40-yard dash]], tied for ninth among linebackers in the [[bench press]], and finished 17th in the [[three-cone drill]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alfie Crow |date=February 25, 2014 |title=2014 NFL Combine results: Linebacker 40-yard dash and more |url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2014/2/25/5445446/2014-nfl-combine-results-linebacker |access-date=December 7, 2017 |website=bigcatcountry.com}}</ref> On March 24, 2014, Hitchens opted to participate at Iowa's [[pro day]], along with [[C. J. Fiedorowicz]], [[Christian Kirksey]], [[James Morris (American football)|James Morris]], and nine other prospects. He improved upon his 40-yard dash (4.65), 20-yard dash (2.72), and ran positional drills for the scouts and team representatives from 28 NFL teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hawkeye tight end C.J. Fiedorowicz draws attention at NFL pro day |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/amp/6866619 |access-date=December 7, 2017 |website=desmoinesregister.com }}{{Dead link|date=June 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Hitchens was projected to be a seventh round pick or priority [[undrafted free agent]] by the majority of [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts. He was ranked the 31st best outside linebacker prospect in the draft by DraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Hitchens, DS #31 OLB, Iowa |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=108547&draftyear=2014&genpos=OLB |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
====2014====
The [[Dallas Cowboys]] selected Hitchens in the fourth round with the 119th overall pick of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Cowboys were heavily criticized regarding his selection, due to many evaluators projecting him to be a seventh round pick or go undrafted. Cowboys' owner [[Jerry Jones]] explained that they chose him to provide depth behind [[Sean Lee]] after experiencing the loss of Lee the year prior.
Jones also stated they planned on selecting Hitchens in the fourth round ahead of time and his speed, athleticism, and tackling ability were key factors.<ref name="t841">{{cite web | last=MacMahon | first=Tim | title=Why were Cowboys high on Hitchens? | website=ESPN.com | date=2014-05-12 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4727909/why-were-cowboys-high-on-anthony-hitchens | access-date=2024-12-26}}</ref> On June 1, 2014, the Cowboys signed Hitchens to a four-year, $2.65 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $434,864.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2014 |title=Anthony Hitchens: Current Contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/dallas-cowboys/anthony-hitchens-14530/ |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

{{external media 
| video1 =
[http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-rookie-of-the-week/0ap3000000399229/Anthony-Hitchens-pulls-weight-in-win Rookie of the Week: Hitchens pulls weight in win]
| video2 =
[http://www.nfl.com/videos/dallas-cowboys/0ap3000000448330/Week-16-Anthony-Hitchens-highlights Anthony Hitchens' Week 16 Highlights]
}}
When Lee was lost for the season during organized team activities, and the team traded for [[Rolando McClain]], it was decided to make Hitchens learn all three [[linebacker]] positions.<ref name="Cowboys position reviews: LBs">{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |date=2015-01-29 |title=Cowboys position reviews: LBs |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfceast/post/_/id/67297/cowboys-position-reviews-lbs |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He began organized team activities taking reps with the first-team defense, but was soon moved to the backup middle linebacker after Justin Durant returned from a [[hamstring injury]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rookie LB Anthony Hitchens signs contract, focused on getting better not playing behind Durant |url=http://sportsblogs.star-telegram.com/cowboys/2014/06/rookie-lb-anthony-hitchens-signs-contract-focused-on-getting-better-not-playing-behind-durant.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171208231531/http://sportsblogs.star-telegram.com/cowboys/2014/06/rookie-lb-anthony-hitchens-signs-contract-focused-on-getting-better-not-playing-behind-durant.html |archive-date=December 8, 2017 |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=sportsblogs.star-telegram.com}}</ref> He spent the bulk of [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]] at outside linebacker, competing with Justin Durant and [[Kyle Wilber]], before being moved back to middle linebacker. The Dallas Cowboys opted to trade for McClain and have Hitchens compete with him in training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarence Hill |date=August 21, 2014 |title=Rolando McClain returns, but Anthony Hitchens gets first-team work |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nfl/dallas-cowboys/article3870206.html |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=star-telegram.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Jason Garrett]] named Hitchens the back up middle linebacker to McClain to begin the 2014 season.<ref name="Cowboys position reviews: LBs" />

He made his professional regular season debut in the Cowboys' season-opener against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and assisted on one tackle in the 28–17 loss. He made his first career tackle in the closing seconds of the game, helping safety [[Barry Church]] tackle 49ers' running back [[Frank Gore]] who gained five-yards on a short run to seal the win for the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 1–2014: San Francisco 49ers @ Dallas Cowboys |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014090710/2014/REG1/49ers@cowboys |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The following week, Hitchens earned his first career start at weakside linebacker and recorded two combined tackles during a 26–10 victory at the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He started in place of Justin Durant, who suffered a [[groin]] injury in the season-opener against the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shawn Leales |date=September 12, 2014 |title=Dallas Cowboys Injury Report: Team Loses Justin Durant to Groin Injury |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/dfw/news/dallas-cowboys-injury-report-team-loses-justin-durant-to-groin-injury/ |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=CBSlocal.com}}</ref> During a Week 3 matchup at the [[St. Louis Rams]], Hitchens collected a season-high 13 combined tackles and deflected a pass in Dallas' 34–31 victory. He also recorded five combined tackles on special teams. Head coach Jason Garrett named Hitchens the weakside linebacker for the remainder of the season after Justin Durant was placed on injured/reserve after tearing his [[biceps]] in the Cowboys' 20–17 overtime loss to the [[Washington Redskins]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 28, 2014 |title=Cowboys linebacker Justin Durant likely out for season with torn biceps |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2014/10/28/dallas-cowboys-justin-durant-biceps-injury |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=si.com}}</ref> On December 21, 2014, Hitchens made eight solo tackles, defended two passes, and has his first career [[interception]] after picking off a pass attempt by [[Indianapolis Colts]] quarterback [[Matt Hasselbeck]] during the Cowboys' 42–7 victory. He was nominated for the Pepsi Rookie of the Week award after his week 16 performance against the Colts.  He finished the regular season with 75 combined tackles (59 solo), four [[pass deflections]], and one interception in 16 games and nine starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player Profile: Anthony Hitchens |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyhitchens/2543592/profile |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

The Dallas Cowboys finished atop the [[NFC East]] with a 12–4 record. On January 4, 2015, Hitchens played in his first career playoff game and recorded three combined tackles and deflected a pass, as the Cowboys defeated the [[Detroit Lions]] 24–20 in the [[NFL Wild card|wildcard playoff]] game against the [[Detroit Lions]]. Hitchens was involved in a heavily controversial play during the fourth quarter after the back judge threw a flag and penalized Hitchens for pass interference for making contact and pushing off of Lions' tight end [[Brandon Pettigrew]] as he attempted to catch a deep pass by [[Matt Stafford]]. The line judge ultimately chose to overturn the penalty and the flag was disregarded without an immediate explanation on the field. After the game, referee [[Pete Morelli]] stated that the line judge determined there was not enough contact to warrant a penalty.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fix Sports |date=January 4, 2015 |title=Ref explains non-PI call at heart of Lions-Cowboys controversy |url=https://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/dallas-cowboys-detroit-lions-anthony-hitchens-brandon-pettigrew-overturning-call-010415%3famp=true |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=foxsports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Todd Archer |date=January 5, 2015 |title=Pete Morelli: Penalty not warranted |url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nfl/story/_/id/12121292/referee-pete-morelli-explains-overturned-pass-interference-call-dallas-cowboys-detroit-lions-wild-card-game |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> The next game, he collected six combined tackles during a 26–21 loss at the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the [[National Football Conference|NFC]] Divisional Round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers – January 11th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201501110gnb.htm |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2015====
Hitchens was slated to become the strong side linebacker after the departure of [[Bruce Carter (American football)|Bruce Carter]], but was switched to middle linebacker after McClain was suspended for the first four games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fox Sports |date=June 2, 2015 |title=No shortage of backup plans in wake of Rolando McClain's suspension |url=https://www.foxsports.com/southwest/story/no-shortage-of-backup-plans-in-wake-of-rolando-mcclain-s-suspension-070215 |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=foxsports.com}}</ref> He was named the starting middle linebacker, ahead of [[Jasper Brinkley]], to begin the regular season.

In Week 2, Hitchens recorded five combined tackles and made his first career sack on [[Philadelphia Eagles]] quarterback [[Sam Bradford]] during a 20–10 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 2-2015: Dallas Cowboys @ Philadelphia Eagles |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2015092012/2015/REG2/cowboys@eagles |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 4, 2015, he recorded a season-high 11 combined tackles and sacked [[Drew Brees]] in Dallas' 26–20 loss at the [[New Orleans Saints]]. On December 19, 2015, Hitchens started at middle linebacker in place of McClain who suffered an injury and collected ten combined tackles during a 19–16 loss to the [[New York Jets]]. He finished the 2015 season with a total of 67 combined tackles (40 solo), two sacks, and a defended pass in 16 games and nine starts as the Cowboys finished 4–12. His production was slightly decreased due to the return of Lee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Hitchens (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyhitchens/2543592/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2016====
Hitchens began training camp competing with [[Kyle Wilber]] and [[Damien Wilson]] for the role as the strongside linebacker.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys' depth chart: 07/01/2016 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/185/DAL |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> He took over the role as the Cowboys' starting middle linebacker after McClain was dealt a ten-game suspension after violating the performance-enhancing drugs policy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jean-Jacques Taylor |date=June 1, 2016 |title=Anthony Hitchens capable of replacing Rolando McClain for Cowboys |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4751905/anthony-hitchens-capable-of-replacing-rolando-mcclain |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jim Wilson |date=July 1, 2016 |title=The Pros & Cons Of Anthony Hitchens Replacing Rolando McClain In The Cowboys Defense |url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2016/7/8/12125772/the-pros-cons-of-anthony-hitchens-replacing-rolando-mcclain-in-the-dallas-cowboys-defense |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=bloggingtheboys.com}}</ref>

He started the Cowboys' season-opener at the [[New York Giants]] and collected six combined tackles in their 20–19 loss. On December 1, 2016, Hitchens recorded a season-high ten combined tackles, deflected a pass, and sacked [[Minnesota Vikings]] quarterback [[Sam Bradford]], as the Cowboys won 17–15. He finished the season with 78 combined tackles (39 solo), 1.5 sacks, and a pass deflection in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Hitchens (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyhitchens/2543592/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The Dallas Cowboys received a playoff berth after finishing atop the NFC East with a 13–3 record. On January 15, 2017, Hitchens started his first career playoff game and collected seven combined tackles in a 34–31 loss at the Packers in the NFC Divisional Round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Green Bay Packers at Dallas Cowboys – January 15th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701150dal.htm |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2017====
He received a considerable raise for the 2017 season after playing over 35% of the Dallas Cowboys' defensive snaps. His salary went from $690,000 to $1.84 million after qualifying for the Proven Performance Escalator. The Proven Performance Escalator was added to the rookie wage scale as a part of the [[collective bargaining agreement]] in 2011 and applies to players who were drafted in the third to seventh round.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |date=January 27, 2017 |title=Anthony Hitchens earns raise of more than $1 million |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4758010/anthony-hitchens-earns-raise-of-more-than-1-million |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp in 2017, Hitchens competed with [[Jaylon Smith]] to maintain his role as the starting middle linebacker. Hitchens was slated to start the season at middle linebacker, but suffered a [[tibia]]l plateau fracture in the Cowboys' final preseason game against the [[Oakland Raiders]]. He was expected to miss up to eight weeks, but was able to return before Week 5.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=August 30, 2017 |title=Injury roundup: No surgery needed for LB Anthony Hitchens |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000837054/article/injuries-no-surgery-needed-for-lb-anthony-hitchen |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171209100636/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000837054/article/injuries-no-surgery-needed-for-lb-anthony-hitchen |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 9, 2017 |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref> On November 12, 2017, Hitchens recorded ten combined tackles in a 27–7 loss to the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. The following week, he moved over to weakside linebacker after Lee suffered a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hairopoulos |first=Kate |date=November 14, 2017 |title=Cowboys LB Anthony Hitchens plans to do his best Sean Lee impression in place of defensive captain |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboys/2017/11/14/cowboys-lb-anthony-hitchens-plans-best-sean-lee-impression-place-defensive-captain |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=sportsday.dallasnews.com}}</ref> Hitchens went on to collect five combined tackles before suffering a groin injury, in the Cowboys 37–9 loss to the Eagles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Patrol |date=November 19, 2017 |title=LB Anthony Hitchens to undergo MRI on possible groin injury |url=https://www.247sports.com/nfl/dallas-cowboys/Bolt/Dallas-Cowboys-LB-Anthony-Hitchens-to-undergo-MRI-on-possible-groin-injury-110781972/Amp |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=247sports.com}}{{dead link|date=January 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On November 30, 2017, Hitchens recorded a season-high 15 combined tackles in Dallas' 34–15 victory over the Redskins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Hitchens (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyhitchens/2543592/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=December 8, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Hitchens finished the season with 84 combined tackles (55 solo), two pass deflections, and one forced [[fumble]] in 12 games and 12 starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Hitchens (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyhitchens/2543592/careerstats |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Hitchens became an unrestricted free agent in 2018 and was considered one of the top free agent linebackers available. He was heavily linked to the Colts due to his experience under defensive coordinator [[Matt Eberflus]] who was his linebacker coach with the Dallas Cowboys. The Dallas Cowboys were interested in re-signing Hitchens, but were unable to offer a considerable contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Hairopoulos |first1=Kate |last2=Machota |first2=Jon |date=March 14, 2018 |title=Anthony Hitchens shares final message with Cowboys, fans as he joins Kansas City Chiefs in free agency |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboys/2018/03/14/will-cowboys-linebacker-cant-re-signfree-agent-anthony-hitchens |access-date=January 11, 2019 |website=sportsday.dallasnews.com}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
====2018====
On March 15, 2018, the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] signed Hitchens to a five-year, $45 million contract that includes $25.09 million and a signing bonus of $14 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=March 13, 2018 |title=Chiefs to sign former Cowboys LB Anthony Hitchens |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-to-sign-former-cowboys-lb-anthony-hitchens-0ap3000000920833 |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 13, 2018 |title=Chiefs begin defensive rebuild with Anthony Hitchens |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/13/chiefs-begin-defensive-rebuild-with-anthony-hitchens/ |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2018 |title=Chiefs Sign Linebacker Anthony Hitchens |url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Sign-Linebacker-Anthony-Hitchens/f214b174-db2b-4a2e-a52d-b8963fc8bfa9 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316042116/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Sign-Linebacker-Anthony-Hitchens/f214b174-db2b-4a2e-a52d-b8963fc8bfa9 |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 16, 2018 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref> Hitchens entered training camp slated as a starting inside linebacker and replaced [[Derrick Johnson]]. Head coach [[Andy Reid]] named Hitchens and [[Reggie Ragland]] the starting inside linebackers to begin the regular season. They began the season alongside outside linebackers [[Dee Ford]] and [[Justin Houston]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Charles |date=September 4, 2018 |title=Chiefs release 1st unofficial depth chart of regular season |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/04/chiefs-release-1st-unofficial-depth-chart-of-regular-season/ |access-date=January 11, 2019 |website=chiefswire.usatoday.com}}</ref>

{{external media 
| video1 =
[http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-game-highlights/0ap3000000970568/Anthony-Hitchens-stops-Yeldon-in-his-tracks-for-loss Anthony Hitchens stops Yeldon in tracks for a loss]
}}
He started in the Chiefs season-opener at the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] and collected a season-high 14 combined tackles (six solo) during a 38–28 victory. In Week 6, he tied his season-high of 14 combined tackles (six solo) as the Chiefs lost 43–40 at the [[New England Patriots]]. In Week 8, Hitchens sustained a rib injury during the fourth quarter of a 30–23 victory against the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2018 |title=Anthony Hitchens questionable to return with rib injury |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nfl/anthony-hitchens-questionable-to-return-with-rib-injury/ar-BBPjZlu |access-date=January 11, 2019 |website=msn.com}}</ref> The following week, he aggravated his rib injury and was subsequently sidelined for the Chiefs' Week 10 victory against the [[Arizona Cardinals]]. Hitchens finished the [[2018 NFL season]] with a career-high 135 combined tackles (81 solo) and forced one fumble in 15 games and 15 starts.<ref name="career" /> His 135 tackles led the Kansas City Chiefs' defense and finished fifth among all players in 2018. He received an overall grade of 40.6 from [[Pro Football Focus]], which ranked 92nd among all linebackers in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Hitchens |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/anthony-hitchens/8754 |access-date=January 11, 2019 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2019====
In Week 7 against the Broncos, Hitchens recorded a team high 6 tackles and sacked [[Joe Flacco]] twice in the 30–6 win. One of his sacks resulted in a forced fumble which teammate Reggie Ragland returned for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2019 |title=Patrick Mahomes hurts knee in Chiefs' win over Broncos |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127902 |access-date=October 17, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Hitchens helped the Chiefs reach [[Super Bowl LIV]] where they defeated the 49ers 31–20. Hitchens recorded four combined tackles in the Super Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LIV – San Francisco 49ers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 2nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202002020kan.htm |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2020====
Hitchens was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Chiefs on December 22, 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lane |first=Mark |date=December 22, 2020 |title=Chiefs LB Anthony Hitchens placed on COVID-19 reserve |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/22/chiefs-anthony-hitchens-covid-19-reserve/ |access-date=February 5, 2021 |website=USAToday.com}}</ref> and activated on January 11, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=January 11, 2021 |title=Chiefs activate Anthony Hitchens, Mike Danna off COVID-19 list |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/01/11/chiefs-activate-anthony-hitchens-mike-danna-off-covid-19-list/ |access-date=February 5, 2021 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref> Hitchens helped the Chiefs reach [[Super Bowl LV]], but lost 31–9 to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. Hitchens recorded 1 tackle in the loss.

====2021====
Hitchens entered the 2021 season as the starting middle linebacker. He started 15 games, finishing second on the team with 80 tackles. He was released on February 22, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chiefs Release LB Anthony Hitchens |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-release-lb-anthony-hitchens |website=Chiefs.com |date=February 22, 2022 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-date=January 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230110181337/https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-release-lb-anthony-hitchens |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Anthony Dion Denham Jr.''' (born July 21, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]] and was signed by the [[Houston Texans]] as an undrafted free agent in 2014.

==Early life==
Denham is the son of Anthony Denham Sr. and Dana Lewis. He spent his high school years in foster care. At [[Woodrow Wilson High School (Los Angeles)|Woodrow Wilson]] high school in Los Angeles, California, he had four letters in football, two in basketball and one in track. He was the team's leading receiver and team captain in three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/anthony_denham_757024.html |title=Anthony Denham Bio - the Official Athletic Site of the University of Utah |accessdate=December 4, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140629184317/http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/anthony_denham_757024.html |archivedate=June 29, 2014 }}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman year, at [[East Los Angeles College]], he set school records for receiving yards and touchdowns with 1,186 yds and 16 touchdowns. In his sophomore 2010 season, his play got caught in a downward spiral, though he still finished second in the American Mountain Conference with 40 catches for 475 yds and 7 touchdowns. Even after his decline, he was still rated as a four star recruit by scout.com and rivals.com. After the 2010 season, he transferred to the [[University of Utah]]. In 2011, he redshirted, and in 2012 his play was limited, finishing with 11 catches for 135 yds. In 2013, his senior year, he started 10 games and had 24 catches for 291 yds and two touchdowns for the [[Utah Utes football|Utes]].

'''Anthony Louis Nicholas Chickillo''' (born December 10, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]] and was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the sixth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[New Orleans Saints]] and [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life==
Chickillo attended [[Gaither High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]] prior to transferring to [[Braulio Alonso High School]], which is also in Tampa, before his junior year. As a senior, he had 140 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], 18 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] and two [[interceptions]]. Chickillo was named the MVP of the 2011 [[Under Armour All-America Game]] after he recorded 1.5 sacks and a [[fumble]] recovery.<ref name="y725">{{cite web | last=Long | first=Corey | title=Long: UA All-America Game notebook | website=ESPN.com | date=2011-01-05 | url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/news/story?id=5994262 | access-date=2024-11-23}}</ref> He was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a four-star recruit and was ranked as the third best [[defensive end]] in his class.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Anthony-Chickillo-101433|title=Anthony Chickillo|work=yahoo.com|access-date=May 4, 2015}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Miami]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/news/story?id=5551607|title=Anthony Chickillo follows heart, family to Miami|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 4, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==
Chickillo played at Miami from 2011 to 2014. He entered his freshman season as a backup before becoming a starter. After three games, he became a starter and would start the next 47 games through his senior year. He finished his career with 170 tackles and 15.5 sacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/shrine-game-gives-anthony-chickillo-another-chance-to-shine-at-trop/2213963/|title=Shrine Game gives Anthony Chickillo another chance to shine at Trop|work=Tampa Bay Times|access-date=May 4, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://caneswatch.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2015/01/20/anthony-chickillo-seems-happy-to-leave-miami-hurricanes-defensive-system/|title=Anthony Chickillo seems happy to leave Miami Hurricanes defensive system – Canes Watch|work=palmbeachpost.com|access-date=May 4, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Coming out of college, Chickillo was projected by some analysts to be a fourth to sixth-round draft pick. He was rated the 13th-best defensive end out of the 148 available by NFLDraftScout.com. Many scouts were divided on what position he was best suited for and classified him as a tweener. He received mostly mixed reviews from analysts and was thought to be a future rotational defensive end.<ref name="draft"/> Chickillo was invited to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] and was able to participate in the full workout and complete all the positional drills. He also attended Miami's [[Pro Day]] but was satisfied with his combine performance and only did positional workouts.<ref name="scout">{{cite web|url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=119368&draftyear=2015&genpos=DE| title=Anthony Chickillo, DS #13 DE, Miami: 2015 NFL Draft| access-date=December 9, 2016| website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
====2015====
On May 2, 2015, Chickillo was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the sixth round (212th overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers select LB Anthony Chickillo in the Sixth Round|url=http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/Steelers-select-LB-Anthony-Chickillo-in-the-Sixth-Round/bd4f60c9-2d77-40e7-869c-49dbb0340097|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226073938/http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/Steelers-select-LB-Anthony-Chickillo-in-the-Sixth-Round/bd4f60c9-2d77-40e7-869c-49dbb0340097|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 26, 2017|website=Steelers.com|date=May 2, 2015|access-date=July 3, 2017}}</ref> Chickillo was the 24th defensive end drafted in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 11, 2015, the Steelers signed Chickillo to a four-year, $2.37 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $73,700.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Anthony Chickillo contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/pittsburgh-steelers/anthony-chickillo-16938/ |access-date=October 11, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=CAP Steelers Salary Cap: Looking Ahead At The Walton, Chickillo And Holliman Rookie Contracts |url=https://steelersdepot.com/2015/05/steelers-salary-cap-looking-ahead-at-the-walton-chickillo-and-holliman-rookie-contracts/ |access-date=October 11, 2018 |author=Bryan, Dave |date=May 2, 2015}}</ref>
{{external media
| video1 =
[https://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-draft/0ap3000000490550/Steelers-pick-Chickillo-No-212 Steelers draft Anthony  Chickillo 212th overall]
}}

On September 6, 2015, he was waived by the Steelers after initially making the 53-man roster. He was signed to the [[practice squad]] three days later. On September 30, 2015, Chickillo was activated from the practice squad to the Steelers' active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers promote linebacker Anthony Chickillo|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-promote-linebacker-anthony-chickillo-15980802|website=Steelers.com|date=September 30, 2015|access-date=January 31, 2017}}</ref>

On October 18, 2015, he appeared in his first career game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]].
He appeared in seven regular-season games for the Steelers in his rookie year, recording six tackles and forcing a fumble. The following week, he recorded his first tackle during a 23–13 loss to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. He had a season-high two tackles and forced a fumble during the Steelers' Week 17 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]]. Chickillo finished his rookie season with a total of six combined tackles and a forced fumble, while appearing in seven regular-season contests and two postseason games.<ref name="NFL">{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/player/anthonychickillo/2552266/profile| title=NFL Player Profile: Anthony Chickillo| access-date=December 9, 2016| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2016====
He began his second season as the third left [[outside linebacker]] on the depth chart behind [[Bud Dupree]] and [[Arthur Moats]].<ref name="ourlads">{{cite web|url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/187/PIT| title=Ourlads.com: Pittsburgh Steelers Depth Chart| access-date=December 9, 2016| website=ourlads.com}}</ref> Although he was mainly featured on special teams, he began to receive more reps as a rotational outside linebacker after Dupree missed the first ten games due to an abdominal injury.

On October 9, 2016, Chickillo recorded three solo tackles, a forced fumble, and his first career sack on [[New York Jets]]' quarterback [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]], during the Steelers' 31–13 victory. The following week, he earned his first career start against the [[Miami Dolphins]] and finished the loss with three solo tackles. During a Week 9 13–21 loss to the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Chickillo made a season-high six combined tackles and was credited with a half a sack on [[Joe Flacco]]. The next game, he made a total of four tackles, forced a fumble, and sacked [[Dak Prescott]] during a 30–35 loss to the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref name="NFL"/>

====2017====
On February 14, 2017, the Steelers signed Chickillo to a one-year, $615,000 restricted free agent tender.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers Re-Sign Exclusive Rights Free Agent OLB Anthony Chickillo|url=https://www.steelersdepot.com/2017/02/steelers-re-sign-exclusive-rights-free-agent-olb-anthony-chickillo/|author=Bryan, Dave|website=SteelersDepot.com|date=February 14, 2017}}</ref> He returned as the Steelers' third left outside linebacker behind Dupree and Moats, but began the regular season featured on special teams.

On September 10, in the season-opening 21–18 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]], Chickillo had two sacks. In addition, [[Tyler Matakevich]] blocked a [[Punt (gridiron football)|punt]], which Chickillo recovered in the end zone for his first career [[touchdown]] and gave the Steelers their first points of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100cle.htm|title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns - September 10th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=September 14, 2017}}</ref>

====2018====
On March 13, 2018, the Steelers extended an original round tender offer to Chickillo as a restricted free agent. On April 21, 2018, Chickillo officially signed his one-year, $1.90 million contract.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Chickillo signs his RFA tender with Steelers |url=https://steelerswire.usatoday.com/2018/04/21/anthony-chickillo-signs-his-rfa-tender-with-steelers/ |access-date=October 11, 2018 |website=SteelersWire.USAToday.com |author=Chester, Simon |date=April 21, 2018}}</ref>

====2019====
On March 12, 2019, Chickillo signed a two-year, $8 million contract extension with the Steelers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers re-signing Anthony Chickillo|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/03/12/steelers-re-signing-anthony-chickillo/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=March 12, 2019}}</ref> After he was arrested for [[domestic violence]] on October 20, 2019,<ref>{{cite news |author=Conroy, Anthony and Jonathan D. Silver |title=Steelers' Anthony Chickillo arrested for assault in Fayette County, told by team to stay home Monday |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/news/crime-courts/2019/10/20/Steelers-linebacker-Anthony-Chickillo-arrested-for-assault-in-Fayette-County/stories/201910200206 |website=Post-Gazette.com |date=October 20, 2019 |access-date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> he was placed on the exempt/commissioner's permission list on October 23, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |author=Varley, Teresa |title=Chickillo placed on exempt list; Elliott signed |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/chickillo-placed-on-exempt-list-elliott-signed |website=Steelers.com |date=October 23, 2019 |access-date=October 23, 2019 |archive-date=October 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191023200953/https://www.steelers.com/news/chickillo-placed-on-exempt-list-elliott-signed |url-status=dead }}</ref> The domestic violence charges were withdrawn on October 30, and he was brought back to the active roster on October 31.<ref>{{cite news |author=Pryor, Brooke |title=Steelers' Anthony Chickillo removed from commissioner's exempt list |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/27973771/steelers-anthony-chickillo-removed-commissioner-exempt-list |website=ESPN.com |date=October 31, 2019 |access-date=October 31, 2019}}</ref> On March 16, 2020, Chickillo was released.<ref>{{cite news |author=Varley, Teresa |title=Steelers make multiple roster moves |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-multiple-roster-moves-x9748 |website=Steelers.com |date=March 16, 2020 |access-date=March 16, 2020}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On May 26, 2020, Chickillo signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=May 21, 2020 |title=Anthony Chickillo signs one-year deal with Saints |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/05/21/anthony-chickillo-signs-one-year-deal-with-saints/ |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> He was released on September 5, 2020, and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Saints announce 53-man roster reductions for 2020 |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-2020-nfl-roster-cuts-53-man |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2020 |title=New Orleans Saints announce practice squad additions |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-practice-squad-additions-2020-roster |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On September 18, 2020, the [[Denver Broncos]] signed Chickillo off the Saints' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign OLB Anthony Chickillo from New Orleans' practice squad|author=DiLalla, Aric|date=September 18, 2020|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-olb-anthony-chickillo-from-new-orleans-practice-squad|website=DenverBroncos.com|access-date=September 18, 2020}}</ref>
In Week 6 against the [[New England Patriots]], Chickillo recorded his first sack as a Bronco on [[Cam Newton]] during the 18–12 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at New England Patriots - October 18th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010180nwe.htm |access-date=2020-10-22 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Chickillo announced his retirement from professional football on July 11, 2021.<ref name="j103">{{cite web | title=Former Steelers LB Anthony Chickillo announces retirement | website=NFL.com | date=2021-07-11 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/former-steelers-lb-anthony-chickillo-announces-retirement | access-date=2024-11-23}}</ref>

'''Anthony Wesly Florence''' (born December 11, 1966) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[defensive back]]. He spent two seasons with the [[National Football League]] (NFL)'s [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and another season with the [[Cleveland Browns]].

Florence was selected in the fourth round of the [[1989 NFL draft]] out of [[Bethune–Cookman Wildcats football|Bethune-Cookman]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=1989 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1989/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> where he was teammates with [[Terry Williams (defensive back)|Terry Williams]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Buccaneers Take Gamble on the 'Unknown Torpedo' |work=[[Sarasota Herald-Tribune]] |date=May 2, 1989 |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1755&dat=19890502&id=BDAeAAAAIBAJ&sjid=NL0EAAAAIBAJ&pg=6586,1619949 }}</ref> The pick was considered a “reach,”<ref>{{cite news |title=Bucs' 4th-round 'Reach' Is Twice As Determined |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=April 30, 1989 |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1989/04/30/bucs-4th-round-reach-is-twice-as-determined/ }}</ref> and Florence never played a down for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers|Buccaneers]].

'''Anthony Ray Denman''' (born October 30, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Cleveland Browns]] and [[Buffalo Bills]]. He was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the seventh round of the [[2003 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]].<ref name="A">{{cite web|url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/denm00200.html |title=ANTHONY DENMAN |publisher=profootballarchives.com |access-date=December 31, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304131410/http://www.profootballarchives.com/denm00200.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Denman earned four [[Letterman (sports)|letters]] playing [[high school football]] at [[Rusk High School]] in [[Rusk, Texas]].<ref name="A"/> He spent time at [[running back]], [[quarterback]], linebacker, [[defensive line]] and [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] during high school. He garnered all-state allocates his senior season in 1996 after rushing for 1,250 yards and 12 touchdowns on offense while recording 85 tackles and one sack on defense. Denman was also team captain as a senior. He earned first-team all-East Texas and all-district honors his junior and senior seasons. He rushed for 1,428 yards and 20 touchdowns as junior in 1995. Denman also earned three letters in [[track and field]].<ref name="C"/>

==College career==
Denman played at the [[University of Notre Dame]] from 1997 to 2000, recording career totals of 207 tackles and nine sacks. He earned [[Associated Press]] second-team [[All-American]] honors in 2000. He was also the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Fighting Irish]]'s MVP and a team captain his senior year in 2000.<ref name="C">{{cite web|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/denman_anthony00.html |title=ANTHONY DENMAN |publisher=und.com |access-date=December 31, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151231184246/http://www.und.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/denman_anthony00.html |archive-date=December 31, 2015 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Denman was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] of the NFL in the seventh round with the 213th pick in the [[2001 NFL draft]] and signed with the team on June 7, 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2001/draft.htm |access-date=March 17, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was released by the Jaguars on August 27, 2001.<ref name="B">{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/anthony-denman-player-transactions |title=ANTHONY DENMAN |work=foxsports.com |access-date=December 31, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151231182459/http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/anthony-denman-player-transactions |archive-date=December 31, 2015 }}</ref>

Denman signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] of the NFL on August 28, 2001, and was released by the team on September 2. He was signed to the Browns' practice squad on September 7 and promoted to the active roster on September 19.<ref name="B"/> He played in eleven games for the Browns during the [[2001 NFL season|2001 season]].<ref name="A"/> Denman was released by the Browns on September 1, 2002.<ref name="B"/>

Denman was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] of the NFL on September 3, 2002.<ref name="B"/> He played in sixteen games for the Bills in 2002.<ref name="A"/>

During his junior year, he received an offer from Harvard after sending all the [[Ivy League]] schools game film. He also received an offer from [[Boston College]] but verbally committed to Harvard, solely based on academics, where he was elected a member of the [[Owl Club (Harvard)|Owl Club]]{{cite web|url=http://m.wakefield.wickedlocal.com/news/20160328/wakefields-fabiano-looks-to-go-from-harvard-to-nfl| title=Wakefield's Fabiano looks to go from Harvard to the NFL| access-date=December 6, 2016| website=Wakefield.com| author=Tenorio, Rich| date=March 28, 2016}} ==College career== Fabiano began attending Harvard in 2012 as a freshman and played in 10 games at left tackle that season.
