'''Anthony Paul Firkser''' (born February 19, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Firkser played [[college football]] for the [[Harvard Crimson football|Harvard Crimson]]. He signed with the [[New York Jets]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2017 and has also played for several other NFL teams.

==Early life==
Firkser was born in [[Englishtown, New Jersey]], to Alex and Donna Firkser. He is Jewish, and he and his family belonged to [[Temple Shaari Emeth]] in [[Manalapan Township, New Jersey|Manalapan]], where Firkser celebrated his [[bar mitzvah]].<ref name="timesofisrael1">{{Cite web |last=Silow |first=Andrew |date=May 9, 2013 |title=Local athletes to compete in Israel Games | New Jersey Jewish News |url=https://njjewishnews.timesofisrael.com/local-athletes-to-compete-in-israel-games/ |access-date=January 20, 2020 |website=New Jersey Jewish News}}</ref><ref name="JeremyFine2017">{{Cite web |last=Fine |first=Jeremy |date=August 23, 2017 |title=7 Jewish NFL Stories to Watch in 2017 |url=http://oychicago.com/tmpl-article.aspx?id=28906 |access-date=January 20, 2020 |website=Oy!Chicago}}</ref><ref name="americanisraelite1">{{Cite web |last=Bloom |first=Nate |date=October 3, 2019 |title=Jewz in the Newz |url=https://www.americanisraelite.com/jews_in_the_newz/article_efc542f2-e46d-11e9-8c5c-b79478288b1f.html |access-date=January 20, 2020 |website=American Israelite |archive-date=October 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191006165806/https://www.americanisraelite.com/jews_in_the_newz/article_efc542f2-e46d-11e9-8c5c-b79478288b1f.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Firkser was a multi-sport athlete at [[Manalapan High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2012 |title=Anthony Firkser fields offers from academic elite, leads Manalapan |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2012/anthony-firkser-fields-offers-from-academic-elite-leads-manalapan |access-date=December 5, 2018 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en}}</ref> In basketball, he played [[point guard]], scoring 21.3 points with 7.6 assists per game. Firkser finished his career second in school history with 1,362 points. In his senior year, the Shore Basketball Coaches named Firkser the Shore Conference Co-Player of the Year. He was also named the Shore Conference ‘A’ North Division Offensive Player of the Year and made the all-state team.

Firkser competed at the [[2013 Maccabiah Games]] in Israel as a guard for the 18-and-under gold medal-winning Team USA basketball team. On the team, he played alongside [[Spencer Weisz]].<ref name="timesofisrael1" /><ref name="americanisraelite1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shoam |first=Amir  |date=August 7, 2013 |title=Maccabiah: U.S. Wins Five Basketball Medals |url=http://pjvoice.org/2013/08/07/maccabiah-u-s-wins-five-basketball-medals/#.XiT5KSN7nx8 |access-date=January 20, 2020 |website=The Philadelphia Jewish Voice}}</ref>

Firkser did not begin playing [[high school football|football]] until his sophomore year in high school. During Firkser's three-year high school career, the Manalapan football team went 30–6 and won three consecutive ‘A’ North Division titles. During one stretch, Manalapan had an 18-game winning streak within the division. After a semifinal visit in the state playoffs his sophomore year, Firkser and his teammates played for the NJSIAA Central Jersey title in his junior and senior years.  While at Manalapan, Firkser set career school records in [[football catch|receptions]] (110), receiving yards (2,118) and [[touchdown]] receptions (19). After his senior year, Firkser was named All-Shore Offensive Player of the Year as a senior [[wide receiver]]. He was also a two-time All-Shore first-team selection.<ref name="GMNews Archive">{{Cite web |last=Morris |first=Tim |date=August 14, 2013 |title=Firkser excelled in both football and basketball |url=http://www1.gmnews.com/2013/08/14/firkser-excelled-in-both-football-and-basketball/ |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=GMNews Archive}}</ref>

==College career==
Firkser was recruited by [[Harvard University]] and four other universities. Citing the university's academic program and the school's willingness to let him play both basketball and football, Firkser committed to play for coach [[Tim Murphy (American football coach)|Tim Murphy]] at Harvard on October 17, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Firkser, Recruiting Activity |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/171224/anthony-firkser |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Firkser saw his first collegiate action in 2014 as a sophomore.  He appeared in 10 games for Harvard and made 32 catches for 485 yards. His four touchdown receptions tied for first on the team and he ranked second on the team in both catches and yards. After the season, Firkser was named to the All-[[Ivy League]] second-team.  Firkser started nine games and caught 22 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in 2015 as a junior. For the second consecutive season, he was named to the All-Ivy League second-team. As a senior in 2016, Firkser started all 10 games for Harvard and made 45 receptions for 702 yards and seven touchdowns.  He was named to the All-Ivy League first-team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Firkser - 2016 - Football |url=https://gocrimson.com/sports/football/roster/anthony-firkser/2163 |access-date=July 20, 2023 |website=Harvard University |language=en}}</ref>

At the end of his collegiate career, Firkser ranked 12th all-time in school history in receptions, ninth all-time in receiving yards, and sixth all-time in touchdown receptions. He graduated from Harvard in 2017 with a degree in [[applied mathematics]]. During the 2018 offseason, Firkser participated in actuarial credential exams in hopes of potentially pursuing a post-football career as an [[actuary]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web |title=Anthony Firkser, Biography |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/team/players-roster/anthony-firkser/ |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=Tennessee Titans}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Coming into the [[2017 NFL draft]], scouting reports projected Firkser to best fit with a [[National Football League]] (NFL) team in a role of a [[fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]]/[[tight end]] hybrid player. Scouts believed Firkser was tough, intelligent, and relatively athletic. Scouts also praised him for his ability to quickly get into pass routes and adjust to errant throws. However, scouts negatively viewed him as possessing just average size and questioned his strength as a blocker.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Draft Analyst: Anthony Firkser |url=http://draftanalyst.com/anthony-firkser |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=draftanalyst.com |archive-date=September 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902115730/http://draftanalyst.com/anthony-firkser |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 19, 2017, Firkser participated in the Harvard [[Pro Day]], an event at which Harvard football players demonstrate their skills to an audience of [[NFL]] scouts and coaches. Nearly half of the NFL teams attended this event.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Harvard Football Hosts 2017 Pro Day |url=https://www.gocrimson.com/sports/fball/2016-17/releases/20170313nayuol |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=gocrimson.com |archive-date=September 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902084224/https://www.gocrimson.com/sports/fball/2016-17/releases/20170313nayuol |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2019 season====
[[File:Anthony Firkser 2019 12-22.jpg|thumb|Firkser in 2019]]
Firkser began the season as one of four tight ends on the Titans' opening day roster along with veterans [[Delanie Walker]], [[Jonnu Smith]], and [[MyCole Pruitt]]. For the first six weeks of the regular season, Firkser played sparingly and was even a healthy inactive in Week 4. During that six-week span, he caught just one pass for 25 yards. After Walker was later placed on [[injured reserve]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moraitis |first=Michael |date=October 23, 2019 |title=Delanie Walker injury updates: The latest on Titans TE's status for Week 8 |url=https://titansized.com/2019/10/23/delanie-walker-injury-updates-week-8/ |access-date=January 5, 2019 |website=titansized.com}}</ref> Firkser played a larger role in the Titans offense. During Week 10 against the Chiefs, he caught three receptions for 36 yards and his only touchdown of the regular season as the Titans won by a score of 35–32.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Tennessee Titans – November 10th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911100oti.htm |access-date=October 22, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Firkser finished the 2019 season with 14 receptions for 204 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Firkser 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FirkAn00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 29, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Ironically, Firkser's first two career touchdowns were against the Jets and Chiefs – the two teams that had previously waived him.

The Titans finished the regular season with a 9–7 record and were the sixth seed in the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] playoffs. Firkser played his first postseason game on January 4, 2020, against the defending [[Super Bowl LIII|Super Bowl]] champions, the [[New England Patriots]]. In that game, he caught two passes for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 20–13 upset road victory in the [[2019–20 NFL playoffs#AFC: Tennessee Titans 20, New England Patriots 13|Wild Card Round]]. With the touchdown, Firkser became the first player from Harvard to score a touchdown in an NFL postseason game.<ref name="Manalapan">{{Cite web |last=Chung |first=Joshua |date=January 6, 2020 |title=From Manalapan High to the NFL: Hometown fans cheer on Titans' playoff hero Anthony Firkser |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/2020/01/06/anthony-firkser-titans-playoff-catch-manalapan-harvard/2823864001/ |access-date=January 7, 2020 |website=Asbury Park Press}}</ref> Firkser's final reception of the season was also the final touchdown of the Titans' 2019 season. He caught a 22-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter of the [[2019–20 NFL playoffs#AFC: Kansas City Chiefs 35, Tennessee Titans 24|AFC Championship]] in a 35–24 road loss to the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 19, 2020 |title=Mahomes' feet, arms, lift Chiefs to Super Bowl over Titans |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131044 |access-date=January 19, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

'''Anthony LaRue Hutchison''' (born February 4, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Buffalo Bills]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyhutchison/2517119/profile |title=Anthony Hutchison Player Profile |website=nfl.com |access-date=December 19, 2019}}</ref> He was selected as the fifth pick in the tenth round of the [[1983 NFL draft]] by the Bears, the 256th pick overall.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1983/draft.htm |title=1983 NFL Draft Draft Listing |website=pro-football-reference.com |access-date=December 19, 2019}}</ref>

His professional football career ended in 1985, and Hutchinson started a landscaping company in Texas. In December 1989, in one of the nation's first federal prosecutions regarding knowingly hiring [[Alien (law)|illegal aliens]], Hutchinson and one of his employees were convicted of multiple charges related to employing illegal aliens. In March 1990, Hutchinson was sentenced to 60 days in jail, eight months of home detention, and a $2,000 fine.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1990/03/20/Former-NFL-player-sentenced/3340637909200/ |title=Former NFL player sentenced |date=March 20, 1990 |publisher=United Press International |access-date=December 19, 2019}}</ref>

'''Anthony Gordon''' (born August 28, 1997) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]]. He played college football for the [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State Cougars]] and went undrafted in the [[2020 NFL draft]]. He was a member of the [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Kansas City Chiefs]], and [[Denver Broncos]] organizations during his three seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

==Early life==
Gordon attended [[Terra Nova High School (California)|Terra Nova High School]] in [[Pacifica, California]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2014/12/05/ccs-football-playoffs-terra-nova-quarterback-anthony-gordon-leaving-his-mark/|title=CCS football playoffs: Terra Nova quarterback Anthony Gordon leaving his mark|date=December 5, 2014}}</ref> During his career he passed for 8,305 yards and 81 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/article/Anthony-Gordon-From-Terra-Nova-to-tearing-it-up-14451097.php|title=Anthony Gordon: From Terra Nova to tearing it up at Washington State|first=Mitch|last=Stephens|date=September 19, 2019|website=SFChronicle.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Gordon played at [[City College of San Francisco]] in 2015. In the one season, he completed 286 of 439 passes for 3,864 yards and 37 touchdowns.

In 2016 he transferred to [[Washington State University]]. He redshirted his first year in 2016 and did not play in any games in 2017. In 2018, he served as the backup to [[Gardner Minshew]]. In 2019, Gordon was named the starter and threw for 48 TDs, second most in the nation behind [[Heisman Trophy]] winner [[Joe Burrow]], who went first overall in the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/aug/30/after-waiting-his-turn-at-washington-state-quarter/|title=After waiting his turn at Washington State, quarterback Anthony Gordon is ready to step into the college football spotlight | The Spokesman-Review|website=www.spokesman.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-football/anthony-gordon-has-waited-on-his-moment-at-wsu-now-hes-ready-to-help-the-cougars-shine/|title=Anthony Gordon waited on his moment at WSU for five years: How this underdog QB won the starting job|date=August 28, 2019|website=The Seattle Times}}</ref>

'''Anthony F. Corvino''' (born September 15, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] and [[Tackle (gridiron football)|tackle]] for one season with the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Southern Connecticut State Owls football|Southern Connecticut State Owls]]. Corvino also played professioallly for three three seasons in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) with the [[Detroit Drive]], [[Washington Commandos]], and [[Connecticut Coyotes]].

==Early life and education==
Corvino was born on September 15, 1965 in [[Beacon Falls, Connecticut|Beacon Falls, CT]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Corvino Pro Football Stats, Position, College, Draft |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/c/corv00200.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=www.profootballarchives.com}}</ref> He attended [[H. Frank Carey Junior-Senior High School]] in [[Franklin Square, New York]], graduating in 1983. He committed to [[Southern Connecticut State Owls football|Southern Connecticut State University]], attending the school for four years: from 1983 to 1986.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerc/corv00200.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Anthony Corvino Stats}}</ref> He was named All-New England as a senior and also [[varsity letter|lettered]] in [[lacrosse]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93051202/the-courier-news/|newspaper=[[The Courier-News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 4, 1987|title=Anthony Corvino}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After graduating, Corvino was signed by the [[New York Jets]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] during the [[1987 NFL strike]]. He was a [[replacement player]], and appeared in two games as a substitute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CorvAn20.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Anthony Corvino Stats}}</ref> He wore number 67, and played tackle and guard.<ref name="auto"/> He was released at the end of the strike.

In 1988, he played for the semi-professional [[Brooklyn Mariners]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93051329/daily-news/|newspaper=[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 11, 1988|title=Mariners head to semi|author=Travers, Bill}} {{Open access}}</ref> They played the [[Racine Raiders]] in the national semi-pro championship,{{efn|Also called the "Semi-Pro [[Super Bowl]]."}} losing 3–5.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93055970/the-journal-times/|newspaper=[[The Journal Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 27, 1988|title=Raiders reign in rain|author=Kabelowski, Art}} {{Open access}}</ref>

Corvino returned to the professional ranks in 1989, playing for the [[Detroit Drive]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). He appeared in two games as they won the [[ArenaBowl III|Arena championship game]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-corviant001|website=Stats Crew|title=Anthony Corvino football statistics}}</ref> He left the Drive in {{AFL Year|1990}} for the [[Washington Commandos]]. With the Commandos, he appeared in just one game, making one [[quarterback sack|sack]].<ref name="auto1"/>

After spending five years out of professional football, Corvino returned in {{AFL Year|1995}} with the [[Connecticut Coyotes]] in the Arena League, making the final roster.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93051442/hartford-courant/|newspaper=[[Hartford Courant]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=May 10, 1995|title=Coyotes make final cuts; Reese says|author=Hasty, Roy}} {{Open access}}</ref> He played in five total games with them, making 5.5 tackles.<ref name="auto1"/>

'''Anthony Christopher Johnson Jr.''' (born December 2, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Chicago Bears]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]], and was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the [[2023 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Johnson Jr. grew up in [[St. Petersburg, Florida]] and attended [[St. Petersburg High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pff.com/news/draft-iowa-state-safety-anthony-johnson-jr-flying-up-pff-draft-board-2023|title=Why Iowa State safety Anthony Johnson Jr. is flying up PFF's draft board|first=Dalton|last=Wasserman|website=[[Pro Football Focus]]|date=April 25, 2023|access-date=April 28, 2023}}</ref> He was rated a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Iowa State over an offer from South Florida.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoyt |first=Joseph |date=May 19, 2017 |title=Football: Cyclones get third commitment in three days, add verbal from Anthony Johnson Jr. |url=https://www.amestrib.com/story/sports/college/football/2017/05/19/football-cyclones-get-third-commitment/20832821007/ |access-date=April 28, 2023 |website=[[Ames Tribune]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Johnson played cornerback for his first four seasons with the Iowa State Cyclones and became a starter during his freshman year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/how-49ers-qb-brock-purdy-influenced-iowa-state-teammate-anthony-johnson|title=Purdy's Iowa State teammate shares what he learned from 49ers QB|first=Jennifer Lee|last=Chan|website=[[NBC Sports Bay Area]]|date=March 2, 2023|access-date=April 28, 2023}}</ref> As a senior, he was named honorable mention [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12 Conference]] after making 55 tackles with three tackles for loss, four passes broken up, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.com/cyclone-football/iowa-states-anthony-johnson-leading-the-way-after-shift-from-cornerback-to-safety/|title=Iowa State's Anthony Johnson 'leading the way' after shift from cornerback to safety|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]|date=May 6, 2022|access-date=April 28, 2023}}</ref> Johnson used the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes due to the COVID-19 pandemic and returned to Iowa State for a fifth season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/football/2021/12/08/iowa-state-cyclones-football-cornerback-anthony-johnson-jr-return-2022-season/6436351001/|title=Iowa State starting cornerback Anthony Johnson Jr. skips NFL Draft, will return for the 2022 season|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=December 8, 2021|access-date=April 28, 2023}}</ref> He moved to safety entering his final season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2022/09/13/iowa-state-football-anthony-johnson-safety-position-change-helping-secondary-2022/10365176002/|title=Iowa State defense boosted by Anthony Johnson after switch to safety|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=September 13, 2022|access-date=April 28, 2023}}</ref> Johnson was named second team All-Big 12 after finishing the year with 60 tackles, two interceptions, and four passes broken up.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4401724/2023/04/12/nfl-draft-iowa-state-prospects/|title=Breaking down Iowa State Cyclones’ 2023 NFL Draft prospects: Where could they end === Green Bay Packers ===
Johnson was selected in the seventh round, 242nd overall, by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.packers.com/news/2023-nfl-draft-packers-select-iowa-state-s-anthony-johnson-in-seventh-round-no-2|title=2023 NFL Draft: Packers select Iowa State S Anthony Johnson Jr. in seventh round, No. 242 overall |website=packers.com |access-date=April 29, 2023|date=April 29, 2023}}</ref> The pick had originally belonged to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], but was traded to the Packers in August 2022 for offensive lineman [[Cole Van Lanen]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 24, 2022 |title=Packers trade T/G Cole Van Lanen to the Jacksonville Jaguars |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-trade-t-g-cole-van-lanen-to-the-jacksonville-jaguars-2022 |access-date=July 20, 2024 |website=Packers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Johnson signed his rookie contract on May 5.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign eight draft picks|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-eight-draft-picks-2023|website=packers.com |access-date=May 5, 2023|date=May 5, 2023}}</ref>

Johnson would not make his NFL regular season debut until Week 7 in a 17–19 loss against the [[Denver Broncos]]. He only played 15 snaps during the game, 11 of them being on [[special teams]]. Johnson made his first career start in Week 9 against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], covering for injured safety [[Rudy Ford]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Packers list LB Quay Walker, S Rudy Ford as questionable for Sunday {{!}} Week 9 Injury Report |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-rams-injury-report-nov-3-2023 |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=www.packers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> This turned out to be Johnson's "breakout game", where in the fourth quarter, Rams' quarterback [[Brett Rypien]]'s pass intended for receiver [[Cooper Kupp]] was tipped by Packers' cornerback [[Jaire Alexander]], which allowed Johnson to make a play on the ball and come down with the interception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Key to the Game: Next men up step up for Packers' defense |url=https://www.packers.com/news/key-to-the-game-next-men-up-step-up-for-packers-defense |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=www.packers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the game with two pass deflections, one tackle, one interception and played every defensive snap as Green Bay went on to win 20–3.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Green Bay Packers - November 5th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311050gnb.htm |access-date=July 20, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Johnson's best showing as a rookie came Week 12 on [[NFL on Thanksgiving Day|Thanksgiving Day]] in a 29–22 win over their [[NFC North]] rival [[Detroit Lions]]. He finished with eight total tackles and one pass deflection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions - November 23rd, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311230det.htm |access-date=July 20, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Johnson was released as part of final roster cuts on August 27, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Packers announce roster moves |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-aug-27-2024 |website=Packers.com |date=August 27, 2024}}</ref>

=== New York Giants ===
Johnson was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Giants]] on August 28, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Obermuller |first=Michael |date=2024-08-28 |title=Giants Claim 'Seventh-Round Gem' to Active Roster: Report |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nfl/new-york-giants/waiver-claims-safety-anthony-johnson-packers/ |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=Heavy.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was active for 9 games in the 2024 season, where he was primarily used as a special teams player. He would eventually record 21 snaps on defense, all of them coming in the last two games of the season.

On July 22, 2025, Johnson was waived by the Giants after a failed physical.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salomone |first1=Dan |title=Andrew Thomas, Eric Gray placed on PUP list; Victor Dimukeje on NFI |url=https://www.giants.com/news/andrew-thomas-eric-gray-placed-on-pup-list-victor-dimukeje-on-nfi |website=giants.com |access-date=23 July 2025}}</ref> He cleared waivers the next day, reverting to the [[Physically unable to perform|reserve/PUP]] list on July 23.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Ely |date=2025-07-25 |title=Minor NFL Transactions: 7/23/25 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2025/07/minor-nfl-transactions-7-23-25 |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref> After spending the 2025 season on [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]], Johnson was released by the team on March 10, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salamone |first1=Dan |last2=Citak |first2=Matt |title=2026 New York Giants Free Agency Tracker |url=https://www.giants.com/news/2026-new-york-giants-free-agency-tracker-roster-moves |website=giants.com |access-date=11 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-10 |title=Giants' Anthony Johnson: Waived by New York |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-anthony-johnson-waived-by-new-york/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On May 21, 2026, Johnson signed with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears announce roster moves |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/chicago-bears-announce-roster-moves-may-21-2026 |access-date=2026-05-21 |website=ChicagoBears.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Anthony Gould''' (born April 6, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] and [[return specialist]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State Beavers]] and was selected by the Colts in the fifth round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Gould was born and grew up in [[Leavenworth, Kansas]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=Oregon State's Anthony Gould, raised by an Army mother and toughened by wrestling, thrives at receiver |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2022/09/oregon-states-anthony-gould-raised-by-an-army-mother-and-toughened-by-wrestling-thrives-at-receiver.html |website=Oregon Live |date=22 September 2022 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> He attended [[West Salem High School (Salem, Oregon)|West Salem High School]] in [[Salem, Oregon]], where he played football. Gould caught 58 passes for 1,191 yards, and 12 touchdowns, while also being a threat on the ground rushing for 744 yards and seven touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Gould Football Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/or/salem/west-salem-titans/athletes/anthony-gould/football/stats/?careerid=51gij73sjaiff |website=MaxPreps.com |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> He committed to play college football at [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State University]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Martini |first1=Pete |title=West Salem's Anthony Gould commits to Oregon State, saying Beavers 'feel like home' |url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/23/west-salem-football-player-anthony-gould-commits-oregon-state-beavers/440750002/ |website=Statsman Journal |date=23 March 2018 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
In his first two seasons Gould played in eight games, returning one punt for 14 yards. He took a redshirt as a freshman after playing four games.<ref>{{cite web |title=2022 Football Roster |url=https://osubeavers.com/sports/football/roster/anthony-gould/9180 |website=OSU Beavers |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> However, Gould stepped up in [[2021 Oregon State Beavers football team|2021]]. In week 2 win versus [[2021 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football team|Hawaii]], he brought in seven receptions for 119 yards and his first career touchdown.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=Chance Nolan, Anthony Gould, running game get Oregon State's offense back on track in 45-27 win over Hawaii |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2021/09/chance-nolan-anthony-gould-running-game-get-oregon-states-offense-back-on-track-in-45-27-win-over-hawaii.html |website=Oregon Live |date=12 September 2021 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> In week 7, Gould got his first rushing touchdown, as he took a sweep 14 yards for a touchdown in a 42–34 win over [[2021 Utah Utes football team|Utah]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=Oregon State rallies to beat Utah 42-34, remains tied for 1st in Pac-12 North: Game at a glance |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2021/10/oregon-state-rallies-to-beat-utah-42-34-remains-tied-for-1st-in-pac-12-north-game-at-a-glance.html |website=Oregon Live |date=24 October 2021 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> He finished the 2021 season with 13 receptions for 185 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martini |first=Pete |date=November 22, 2022 |title=NFL potential? West Salem grad Anthony Gould is a playmaker for Oregon State |url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/college/oregon-state/2022/11/22/anthony-gould-wide-receiver-has-become-a-playmaker-for-oregon-state-beavers-college-football/69597578007/ |access-date=30 July 2023 |website=Statesman Journal}}</ref>

Gould had a breakout season in [[2022 Oregon State Beavers football team|2022]]. In the season opener he had a 74-yard reception to help set up a touchdown and finished the day with two receptions for 69 yards in a win over [[2022 Boise State Broncos football team|Boise State]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2022 |title=Nolan leads Oregon State to 34-17 victory over Boise State |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/gametracker/recap/NCAAF_20220903_BOISE@OREGST/ |access-date=30 July 2023 |website=CBSSports.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> The next week Gould had another huge catch, a 42-yard reception, to set up a touchdown for Deshuan Fenwick as Oregon State beat [[2022 Fresno State Bulldogs football team|Fresno State]] on the final play of the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oregon State Rallies to Stun Fresno State on Final Play |url=https://www.nationalfootballpost.com/college-football/oregon-st-rallies-to-stun-fresno-st-on-final-play/ |website=National Football Post |date=11 September 2022 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=Rewinding Oregon State Beavers' 35-32 win at Fresno State |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2022/09/oregon-state-beavers-at-fresno-state-football-score-updates-live-stream-odds-time-tv-channel-how-to-watch-online-91022.html |website=Oregon Live |date=11 September 2022 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref>

The following week against [[2022 Montana State Bobcats football team|Montana State]], Gould hauled in five receptions for 77 yards and two touchdowns, along with an 80-yard punt return touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martini |first=Pete |date=September 17, 2022 |title=West Salem grad Anthony Gould has monster game for Oregon State against Montana State |url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/college/oregon-state/2022/09/18/west-salem-grad-anthony-gould-has-monster-game-for-oregon-state-beavers-football/69501627007/ |access-date=30 July 2023 |website=Statesman Journal}}</ref> In Week 11, he hauled in two passes for 49 yards and returned a punt for a 54-yard touchdown.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=Rewinding Oregon State Beavers' 38-10 win over California Bears |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2022/11/oregon-state-beavers-vs-california-bears-football-score-updates-live-stream-odds-time-tv-channel-how-to-watch-online-111222.html |website=Oregon Live |date=12 November 2022 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref>

Gould finished 2022 with 27 receptions for 457 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=Oregon State football: Anthony Gould hopes Beavers' young receivers watch and learn from his example |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2023/04/oregon-state-football-anthony-gould-hopes-beavers-young-receivers-watch-and-learn-from-his-example.html |website=Oregon Live |date=11 April 2023 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> He was named first-team All-Pac-12 and first-team All American, both as a punt returner.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martini |first=Pete |date=December 13, 2022 |title=West Salem grad Anthony Gould named All-American for Oregon State |url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/college/oregon-state/2022/12/13/west-salem-grad-anthony-gould-named-all-american-for-oregon-state/69726007007/ |access-date=30 July 2023 |website=Statesman Journal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Anthony Gould & Damien Martinez add more All-American Honors |url=https://247sports.com/college/oregon-state/article/oregon-state-beavers-anthony-gould-damien-martinez-all-american-199971001/ |access-date=30 July 2023 |website=247Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gehrett |first1=Les |title=OSU football: Gould, Bolden step into bigger roles for Beavers |url=https://gazettetimes.com/sports/beavers-sports/football/osu-football-gould-bolden-step-into-bigger-roles-for-beavers/article_1e0390c6-d4d7-11ed-8ad8-73c00c36613d.html |website=Corvallis Gazette-Times |date=6 April 2023 |access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref>

In [[2023 Oregon State Beavers football team|2023]], Gould played extensively as a wide receiver and a kick return specialist. He played 93% of his snaps from scrimmage as an outside receiver in 2023, as opposed to playing from the slot, and was regarded as one of the Pac-12's best deep threats.<ref name=Denney>Jarrid Denny, "Colts Draft WR Gould at 142," ''Eugene Register-Guard,'' April 28, 2024, p. 4B.</ref> He finished the year with 44 receptions for 718 yards (16.3 yard per catch average) and scored two touchdowns for the Beavers.<ref name=Denney /> He also returned seven punts for 113 yards.<ref name=Denney />

Gould tallied a total score of 75 at the 2024 NFL Scouting Combine, ranking 19th among wide receivers who participated.<ref name=Denney /> His time of 4.39 seconds in the 40-yard dash was the 19th fastest among all Combine participants and his "athleticism" score of 91 was the fourth best among wide outs.<ref name=Denney />

Gould was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the fifth round, 142nd overall, of the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref name=Denney /> Throughout the 2024 season, he mainly served as a return specialist, recording four punt returns for a season-high 109 yards in his Week 1 NFL debut against the [[2024 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Gould 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GoulAn00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-12-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> 

In the 2025 season, Gould's role of return specialist continued. He had two consecutive weeks of over 100 return yards, making three kick returns for 104 yards in Week 3, as well as four kick returns for 91 yards and two punt returns for 31 yards (a combined career-high of 122 return yards in a single game) in Week 4. In 11 appearances (one start) for the Colts, Gould recorded two receptions for six scoreless yards. On December 27, 2025, Gould was placed on season-ending [[injured reserve list|injured reserve]] due to a foot injury suffered in Week 14 against the [[2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Colts place DT DeForest Buckner, TE Drew Ogletree, WR Anthony Gould on injured reserve; activate WR Ashton Dulin from injured reserve|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-place-deforest-buckner-drew-ogletree-anthony-gould-injured-reserve-activate-wr-ashton-dulin-other-roster-moves-for-week-17|access-date=January 21, 2026|website=colts.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Anthony Hill Jr.''' (born February 14, 2005) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and was selected by the Titans in the second round of the [[2026 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Hill was born on February 14, 2005, in [[Wichita, Kansas]], and grew up in [[Denton, Texas]]. He attended [[Billy Ryan High School]], where he played football and competed in the triple jump and the [[4 × 400 metres relay]].<ref>{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=August 14, 2022 |title=2022 preseason all-area defense: Denton Ryan's Anthony Hill is our Player of the Year |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2022/08/14/2022-preseason-all-area-defense-denton-ryans-anthony-hill-is-our-player-of-the-year/ |access-date=August 9, 2023 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> In his first varsity season, he recorded 105 tackles with 11 tackles for loss and three sacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/article252654698.html|title=Texas HS football players headline ESPN 300 juniors list|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=July 9, 2021|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref> Hill was named the MVP of District 5-5A and the All-Area Defensive Player of the Year by the ''[[Denton Record-Chronicle]]'' as a junior after making 131 tackles with 18 tackles for loss and eight sacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hookem.com/story/recruiting/2022/02/03/texas-football-look-texas-longhorns-texas-a-m-aggies-top-10-recruits-2023/9291806002/|title=Texas football: A look at the state's top 10 recruits for 2023|first=Hannah|last=Williford|work=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|date=February 3, 2022|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref> He played in only six games during his senior season due to injury and had 67 tackles, four tackles for loss, two sacks, and five forced fumbles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/No-1-LB-and-former-Texas-A-M-commit-Anthony-Hill-17657690.php|title=No. 1 LB and former Texas A&M commit Anthony Hill Jr. flips to Texas before signing day|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=December 15, 2022|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref> After the season Hill played in the 2023 [[All-American Bowl (high school football)|All-American Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dentonrc.com/sports/high_schools/ryan_raiders/ryan-star-anthony-hill-earning-national-attention-at-all-american-bowl/article_d3fe7095-0d6b-5c02-9526-630519ee3d74.html|title=Ryan star Anthony Hill earning national attention at All-American Bowl|work=[[Denton Record-Chronicle]]|date=January 6, 2023|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref>

Hill was rated a five-star recruit and was ranked as the top linebacker in his class nationally by several major recruiting services.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/texas/article/anthony-hill-five-star-ranking-texas-longhorns-football-recruiti-203653060/|title=Texas linebacker Anthony Hill finishes as five-star in final 247Sports rankings|first=Hudson|last=Standish|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=January 26, 2023|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref> He initially committed to play college football at [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/34319378/espn-300-linebacker-anthony-hill-jr-commits-texas-aggies|title=ESPN 300 LB Anthony Hill Jr. commits to Texas A&M Aggies|first=Blake|last=Baumgartner|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=July 30, 2022|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref> Hill later decommitted and reopened his recruitment during his senior football season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/34972970/anthony-hill-jr-no-2-lb-23-decommits-texas-am|title=Anthony Hill Jr., No. 2 LB in '23, decommits from Texas A&M|first=Blake|last=Baumgartner|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 7, 2022|access-date=August 8, 2023}}</ref> He ultimately chose to sign with [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4007030/2022/12/15/texas-recruiting-anthony-hill-jr/|title=Texas lands 5-star linebacker Anthony Hill Jr.: What he adds to Longhorns' special 2023 class|first=Sam|last=Khan Jr.|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=December 15, 2022|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==

=== 2023 season ===
Hill joined the [[Texas Longhorns football|Longhorns]] as an early enrollee at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in January 2023 in order to take part in the team's spring practices.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/college/longhorns/football/2023/04/16/lb-anthony-hill-impresses-veteran-teammates-coach-at-texas-spring-game/70118087007/|title=Texas spring football notes: Freshman LB Anthony Hill impresses veteran teammates, coach|first=Thomas|last=Jones|work=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|date=April 16, 2023|access-date=August 8, 2023}}</ref> As a freshman, Hill appeared in 14 games with six starts. He totaled 67 tackles, eight tackles for a loss, five sacks, two pass deflections, and one forced fumble. At the end of the season, he was named [[Big 12 Defensive Freshman of the Year]] and [[Freshman All-American]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Anthony Hill Jr. - Football |url=https://texaslonghorns.com/sports/football/roster/anthony-hill-jr/14362 |access-date=September 22, 2025 |website=University of Texas Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2024 season ===
As a sophomore, Hill played and started in all 16 games. Throughout the season, he logged 113 tackles, eight sacks, one interception, and four forced fumbles. Hill was the only Texas defender with 100+ tackles on the season. At the end of the season, Hill was named a first team All-American and first team All-SEC.<ref name=":0" />

{{Short description|American football player (born 1970)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2024}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Anthony Daigle | image = | number = 23 | position = [[Running back]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1970|4|5}} | birth_place = [[San Francisco, California]], U.S. | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 10 | weight_lbs = 203 | high_school = [[St. Patrick-St. Vincent High School|St. Patrick-St. Vincent]]
([[Vallejo, California]]) | college = [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State]] | draftyear = 1994 | draftround = 6 | draftpick = 185 | pastteams = * [[Kansas City Chiefs]] ({{NFL Year|1994}})* * [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] ({{NFL Year|1994}}) * [[Cincinnati Bengals]] ({{NFL Year|1996}})* | pfr = DaigAn20 }} '''Anthony John Daigle''' (born April 5, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for one season with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State]], [[El Camino Junior College]], and [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State]]. He was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the sixth round of the [[1994 NFL draft]]. ==Early life== Anthony John Daigle was born on April 5, 1970, in [[San Francisco, California]].{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/d/daig00100.html | title=Anthony Daigle | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He played [[high school football]] at [[St. Patrick-St. Vincent High School]] in [[Vallejo, California]] as a running back. He scored 21 touchdowns his senior year, earning Cal-Hi Sports Small School Player of the Year honors. He also played basketball and baseball in high school. Daigle was inducted into the Vallejo Sports Hall of Fame in 2008.{{cite web | url=https://www.timesheraldonline.com/2008/03/05/anthony-daigle-the-td-maker/ | title=Anthony Daigle, the TD-maker | publisher=timesheraldonline.com | date=March 5, 2008 | accessdate=23 December 2024 | author=Samano, Simon Jude}} ==College career== Daigle began his college career as a member of the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]] in 1989 and [[redshirted]] that season. He played at [[El Camino Junior College]] in 1990, rushing for 1,276 yards and garnering junior college honorable mention [[All-American]] honors. Daigle was then a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]] from 1991 to 1993.{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-daigle-1.html?__hstc=223721476.cf5f44155f2e36f92dc58b684a6e9a44.1694291523663.1735001526655.1735007567002.999&__hssc=223721476.1.1735007567002&__hsfp=3542455373 | title=Anthony Daigle | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He rushed 102 times for 509 yards and ten touchdowns in 1991 while also catching 11 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown. He totaled 111 carries for 680 yards and a [[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]]-leading 16 touchdowns in 1992. In 1993, he recorded 151 rushing attempts for 755 yards and six touchdowns, and 37 receptions for 543 yards and eight touchdowns. Daigle later graduated from Fresno State with a bachelor's degree in business. ==Professional career== Daigle was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the sixth round, with the 185th overall pick, of the [[1994 NFL draft]]. He signed with the team on July 20.{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/d/daig00100.html | title=Anthony Daigle NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He was waived on August 23 and signed to the team's practice squad on August 31. Daigle was released by the Chiefs on October 19, 1984. Daigle was signed to the practice squad of the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] on October 27, 1994. He was promoted to the active roster on November 24 and played in one game for the Steelers during the 1994 season.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaigAn20.htm | title=Anthony Daigle | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He was waived on August 27, 1995. Daigle signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on February 16, 1996.{{cite web | url=https://prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Anthony+Daigle&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He was waived on August 25, 1996. ==Personal life== Daigle later worked as a personal finance counselor. ==References== {{reflist}} {{Chiefs1994DraftPicks}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Daigle, Anthony}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:1970 births]] [[Category:American football running backs]] [[Category:Arizona State Sun Devils football players]] [[Category:El Camino Warriors football players]] [[Category:Fresno State Bulldogs football players]] [[Category:Kansas City Chiefs players]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Steelers players]] [[Category:Players of American football from San Francisco]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:Cincinnati Bengals players]]

'''Anthony Quinn Coleman''' (born August 20, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor Bears]]. He was signed as a [[replacement player]] during the players strike during the [[1987 NFL season|1987 season]].

As a replacement player, Coleman appeared in three games, on October 4 against the [[1987 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], October 11 against the [[1987 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], and lastly on October 19 against the [[1987 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]]. While appearing in three games, he recorded no statistics.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/anthony-coleman-coleman02 |title=Anthony Coleman Statistics |website=The Football Database |access-date=February 24, 2024}}</ref>
